text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London ended little changed in thin activity. Most-active October finished 20 cents firmer at $322.50 per tonne. December remained unchanged at $319.70 per tonne. Trade buying at the lows helped support October, offsetting selling from other trade players and commission houses.

Raw sugar futures in New York closed barely lower in quiet dealings. There was no fresh news to influence prices. October and March lost 2 points to close at 11.49 and 11.75 cents/lb respectively. The first production estimates for 1997/98 are not likely to show any great surprises.

EUROPE - Western Europe's sugar beet areas reported only light rains during the week ended August 13. Conditions are stable. In Italy 10-25 mm of rains were recorded in the north for the second week in a row which helped maintain good growing conditions. In Spain, soil moisture is declining in the northern producing area.

In Eastern Europe, there was some rainfall during the week ending August 13, but the excessive pattern finally slackened. Surplus soil moisture is still a concern. However, the outlook for this year's crop is stable. Sugar beet areas in the former Soviet Union had near normal rainfall (10-30 mm) during the week ended August 13. The outlook remains for higher yields than last season.

DENMARK - Sugar imports in May 1997 amounted to 7,359 tonnes, raw value, up from 2,406 tonnes imported in May 1996. This brought cumulative imports in the first eight months of 1996/97 (October/May) up to 33,473 tonnes compared to 8,322 tonnes in the like period the previous year.

Total imports in 1995/96 reached 29,387 tonnes against 4,960 tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of origin in 1996/97 were Sweden with 17,501 tonnes whites against 966 tonnes and Germany with 12,309 tonnes compared to 6,107 tonnes.

Sugar exports in May 1997 amounted to 9,310 tonnes, down from 11,876 tonnes in May 1996. This brought cumulative exports in October/May 1996/97 up to 120,452 tonnes compared to 107,215 tonnes in 1995/96. Total exports in 1995/96 amounted to 173,004 tonnes against 199,559 tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of destination in 1996/97 were Norway with 59,482 tonnes whites against 76,714 tonnes, Libya with 30,800 against nil and Iceland with 6,096 tonnes, up from 5,779 tonnes.

DENMARK - No rainfall was recorded in the week ended August 10. Temperatures and the hours of sunshine were above normal. Precipitation levels since April 1 ranged between 177-247 mm compared to an average of 211-222 mm. Growth is still considered to be very good. Diseases and pests are without any significance. Crop prospects are considered to be normal.

UNITED KINGDOM - Sugar imports in May 1997 amounted to 139,416 tonnes, raw value, up from last year's 130,446 tonnes. This brought cumulative imports in the first 8 months of 1996/97 (October/May) up to 866,296 tonnes compared to 932,704 tonnes in 1995/96. Total imports in 1995/96 reached 1.380 million tonnes against 1.635 million tonnes in 1994/95.

Major countries of origin in 1996/97 were Mauritius with 314,760 tonnes raws against 369,852 tonnes, Guyana with 148,673 tonnes, up from 124,696 tonnes and Jamaica with 94,347 tonnes against 87,704 tonnes. The largest white sugar supplier was France with 29,537 tonnes against 14,024 tonnes.

Sugar exports in May 1997 amounted to 38,893 tonnes compared to 34,940 tonnes in May 1996. This brought cumulative exports in October/May 1996/97 up to 255,762 tonnes against 257,230 tonnes in 1995/96. Total exports in 1995/96 reached 390,747 tonnes against 560,076 tonnes in 1994/95.

Major countries of destination in 1996/97 were Israel with 82,799 tonnes whites against 77,060 tonnes, Norway with 21,650 tonnes, down from 31,678 tonnes and Hong Kong with 18,830 tonnes against 14,656 tonnes.

The European Union awarded 16,000 tonnes of white sugar at a maximum refund of ECU 39.857 per 100 kg at its weekly tender on August 13. Cumulative awards so far made under the 1997/98 series of tenders for the period up to August 13 reached 44,000 tonnes, which compares to 56,000 tonnes last year.
Iraq will hold a buying tender of between 25,000 and 50,000 tonnes of white sugar on August 15.
